source.title: Robust and On-the-fly Dataset Denoising for Image Classification
source.authors: Jiaming Song; Lunjia Hu; Y. Dauphin; M. Auli; Tengyu Ma

record.tranche_reason: The study trains residual networks on artificial uniform label noise and measures the resulting clean and noisy example loss distributions, using the same broad noisy-label training intervention as the claim.
record.gate_note: The study reports loss-distribution results for clean and uniformly mislabeled examples. Its validation-accuracy tables, ODD denoising results, and cited findings from prior work do not measure the claim versions and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study's own clean-versus-noisy training-loss comparisons bear on V6: clean examples are learned while uniformly mislabeled examples make little progress at large learning rates. They do not measure eventual fitting of a completely random labeling, as V1 requires.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the motivating loss-separation observation but incompletely summarizes the paper's conclusion. The authors conclude that ODD uses a counterfactual noisy-label loss distribution to prune potentially harmful examples, improves performance on artificial and real noisy datasets, remains competitive on clean datasets, and identifies mislabeled CIFAR-100 examples.
record.recipe_differences: Trains residual networks with SGD on artificially corrupted labels and examines loss distributions at selected epochs; it does not report the original studies' final random-label training-error result.
record.method_sensitivity: The loss separation is reported for large learning rates; the authors state that noisy examples start to be fit when the learning rate decreases further. The amount of random label noise tested is 20% and 40%.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix A.1.3 describes an approximately noise-proportional 'training error,' but explicitly interprets it as the fraction exceeding ODD's loss threshold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At the selected early epoch, ODD's threshold identifies a fraction of examples approximately matching the injected noise fraction; this does not establish classification training error or eventual memorization.

record.problems: The claim-relevant loss distributions are presented in Figure 3 without numerical values or uncertainty. The study does not report final training error on random labels or test error at chance for standard training.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-version results were reported. Validation-accuracy and ODD denoising outcomes do not measure the behaviors named in the versions.

untested.parts: Eventual zero or near-zero training error on completely random labels, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Training-time ratios and convergence speed across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect training fit throughout a corruption sweep extending to fully random labels, together with test error approaching chance. ERM validation accuracy declines over 0%, 20%, and 40% corruption, but the joint training-fit claim is not established.
Whether explicit regularizers prevent random-label fitting and whether removing them preserves clean-label generalization.
The rows do not directly track subsequent memorization of noisy labels after learning-rate reduction; that statement is presented as consistent with prior work.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the V1 limits_scope verdict: a loss gap at selected early epochs does not qualify or contradict eventual random-label fitting. The validation-accuracy and ODD performance results are already declared excluded in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report final training error or test error at chance for a standard model trained to convergence without ODD.
Does not report perfect training error together with test error across a sweep from clean to fully random labels.
The related discussion in the paper cites prior work; it does not test this version.

rows.subject: deep residual networks on CIFAR-100
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD on clean and uniformly randomly mislabeled examples; compared their per-example loss distributions at a specified epoch.

conditions.value: specific epochs; exact epoch not stated

rows.measure: Per-example training-loss distributions for clean and uniformly mislabeled examples
rows.value: The distributions have notable statistical distance; noisy-example loss is relatively stable across the tested noise proportions.
rows.note: The text describes the direction and stability of the distributions but does not give numerical losses or final training error.
rows.check: Relink from V1 to V6. Section 3.1 and Figure 3 show lower losses for clean examples while noisy-example losses remain relatively stable during large-learning-rate training. This is evidence of differential learning, not partial evidence of eventual zero training error.
